title: Ben Johnson on bringing relentless attitude every week | Press Conference
headline: Short-week prep for Thursday vs. New England; Johnson gave no injury or role updates, only that Caleb Williams needs to stack strong performances.
summary: Johnson opened by saying the Bears are finalizing a game plan for a Thursday matchup against a New England team he respects, citing Mike Vrabel's coaching and the team's physical, smart style. He said Caleb Williams had a good performance Sunday, but he played down the idea that sitting out helped him grow, noting similar traits showed up in camp. His message for Williams and the rest of the team is to string good performances together back to back. He described New England's defense as talented and hard to move on the interior, with strong linebackers and edge players who will test the Bears' tackles one-on-one. He also praised Kevin Byard and said the staff is unsure where Christian Gonzalez will line up. On offense, he called Drake Maye a dangerous mix of elite deep-ball throwing and running ability, and said the Patriots' offense has been explosive during a three-game win streak. He credited Dennis Allen's defense for playing faster and tighter in coverage in year two of the system, and said the special teams and defense were swarming and protective of the ball. He stressed that the team must play clean on the short week, because last week's high penalty count would hurt against a good opponent. He gave no injury updates or specific depth chart changes.

signals.note: Johnson called Williams' Sunday performance good but wants consistency, with no sign of a change in his role or workload.

topics.detail: Johnson called the Patriots strong up the middle, with high-level linebackers and good edge players who will test the Bears' tackles one-on-one. He praised Kevin Byard's fit and said it's unclear where Christian Gonzalez will line up.

Drake Maye is an elite deep thrower who can also hurt teams with his legs. The Patriots have won three straight with many explosive plays, and Josh McDaniels does a good job of putting players in the right spots even with offensive line injuries.

Johnson said Dennis Allen's pressure package, especially on third down, is working. He sees players who understand the scheme better, play faster and cover tighter in year two, and he said that leaves less room for quarterbacks to escape.

With a Thursday game, Johnson plans to streamline the game plan and have players play fast and clean. He called last week's penalty total a concern and said the team has to keep up the same relentless effort.
Johnson said backups across the offensive line, receivers, defensive backs and pass rushers get coached up and must be ready. He expressed confidence in them but named no specific players.

title: Campbell on Week 7 preparation
headline: Brian Branch is returning at safety for Week 7 vs. GB, with Chuck Clark and Keith Abney competing to play next to him. Gill-Howard won't see a heavy edge role.
summary: Campbell spent most of the session praising the Packers, who are on a hot streak with a plus-6 turnover margin over the last two games and seven takeaways. He called Jordan Love the 'secret sauce' and said the Love-Watson-Golden trio is a dangerous deep threat. He said roughly half of their deep shots end in a catch or a pass-interference call. He expects the Packers to lean on the run and anticipates Jacobs will be back. He wants the Lions' front to get pressure but stay disciplined, because Love is most dangerous when he extends plays. Campbell likes the matchup with the current Lions front better than in past meetings. He said Skyler Gill-Howard's edge rush was a one-off curveball born of a thin rotation, and he doesn't expect a heavy dose of it. He confirmed Brian Branch is coming back, said Chuck Clark has been steady and Keith Abney will play, and said Branch's versatility lets whoever plays next to him do their job. On 'Kirby' (apparently Kerby Joseph), he gave no timetable and said only that he's in a good head space and it's day to day.

injuries.detail: Campbell said he is coming back and referred to 'getting BB' back at safety for the Packers game.
Asked about 'Kirby' (likely Kerby Joseph, not on the provided roster). Campbell said he's doing well and in a good head space, but gave no timetable and is taking it one day at a time.

signals.claim: Will return to the safety rotation this week and play both deep (top-down) and underneath roles.
signals.note: His return should lift the Lions' defensive back usage and gives IDP managers a versatile safety back in the lineup.
signals.quote: Here's what's great about getting BB. BB gives you the flexibility

signals.claim: Will be part of the safety group alongside Branch and could start at the other safety spot.
signals.note: Campbell praised him as a steady veteran, but he didn't commit to a starter next to Branch.
signals.quote: Chuck has been really steady for us, man. He's smart.

signals.claim: Will play for the Lions at safety and continues to be invested in.
signals.note: Abney has a defined role in the safety rotation, which matters in deeper IDP leagues.
signals.quote: Abney is is worth continuing to invest in. He's going to play for us.

signals.claim: Will not get a heavy dose of snaps rushing off the edge.
signals.note: His edge rush was a situational curveball, so don't expect a bigger pass-rush role from it.
signals.quote: I don't think you're going to see some heavy dose of him out there.

topics.detail: Campbell called Love the 'secret sauce' and the Love-Watson-Golden group dangerous down the field. He said about 50% of their deep shots end in a catch or DPI. He expects Jacobs back and a commitment to the run, with Kraft playing well after injury.
He described a disguise-heavy, opportunistic unit under Gannon with seven takeaways over the last two weeks. He also credited improved offensive line play and strong special teams.
Love is slippery and most dangerous when he buys time, so the Lions need to get to him while staying disciplined. Campbell said he likes the Lions' chances better with their current front.
Campbell stressed that division games count as 'a game and a half' after the Lions went 2-4 in the division last year. He declined to lean into the rivalry and said he respects the Packers.

title: Shanahan Reflects on 6-0 Start, Gritty Finish Over Commanders
headline: Mike Evans' Achilles tendinitis flared up and knocked him out after the first half. Shanahan hopes he plays next week but admits he may not, and Demarcus Robinson won't be ready this week.
summary: Shanahan praised the team's competitive stamina in the 6-0 win over Washington, even though the offense went three-and-out on its last three drives and the defense had to close the game out. Mike Evans played after missing practice all week because of Achilles tendinitis, but it acted up too much and he left at halftime. Shanahan says it isn't expected to be long-term and no more testing is planned, but Evans is week to week and the team may rest him until after the bye if needed. Luke Gifford (groin) and Upton Stout (shoulder) also left and didn't return. That pushed Jalen Graham into more base-defense snaps and Ashtyn Davis into a key role in the fourth quarter. Demarcus Robinson isn't expected back this week, and Shanahan said Deebo Samuel Sr. is likely to return after the bye. A practice-squad receiver was elevated because the group is thin. Shanahan also praised Malik Mustapha and Romello Height, and said a bad punt-return decision will be reviewed.

injuries.detail: Achilles tendinitis that kept him out of practice all week; he left in the second half. Shanahan hopes he can play next week but said the team may wait until after the bye.

topics.detail: After a strong opening drive of the second half, the next three drives ended in three-and-outs. Two sacks and a hot route that got caught up were the main problems. Shanahan said he should have called a run on one second-and-four.

Shanahan said the receiver group is short, a practice-squad receiver was elevated, and the team has enough in the building. Shanahan also mentioned a receiver named Christian who had two good practices and was a close call to play; he is a possibility next week. Another player named Christian was used in the slot and at wideout, and blocked well on run plays.
Shanahan criticized the kicker for another missed extra point and a punt returner for a bad decision to field a punt.
A defensive lineman in his second game back from a long injury recovery got a sack. Shanahan called his return huge and hopes he avoids setbacks.

title: HC Dan Quinn | 10/21/26
headline: Terry McLaurin is out for the season with a torn patellar tendon, so Van Jefferson and other deep-speed WRs should see bigger roles after the bye.
summary: Dan Quinn opened by announcing that Terry McLaurin has a torn patellar tendon, will have surgery and will miss the rest of the season. Quinn called it a gut punch for a captain and leader. He said the receiver room is deep and the team will lean on several players to fill McLaurin's different roles. He named Van Jefferson (excellent camp) and a receiver who sounds like Jaylin Lane (deep plays), and said Treylon Burks has some of the same traits. McLaurin's superpower is contested catches, which others only partly replace. Imaging on other injuries, including Burks, is still ongoing, and Quinn will give updates Monday. After the loss to San Francisco and a 1-5 style start of adversity, the bye week is a self-scout. Quinn expects smaller tweaks, a more streamlined and decisive offense and defense, and no new system, and he warned that players who don't execute could lose reps. He was critical of the offensive line's performance and said the team is still searching for the right interior combination. On Jayden Daniels, he wants more scramble-to-throw plays, more keepers off play action, and better staying through his reads, while praising his elite throws.

injuries.detail: Torn patellar tendon, surgery planned, out for the rest of the season.
Quinn had no update. Imaging is still ongoing, with more news expected Monday.

signals.claim: McLaurin will have surgery and miss the rest of the 2026 season.
signals.note: Season-ending loss of the team's top receiver. Drop him in redraft and expect target redistribution.
signals.quote: he's going to miss the rest of the season

signals.claim: Jefferson will be elevated into a bigger receiver role with McLaurin out.
signals.note: He is the first receiver Quinn named as a likely beneficiary, which makes him a waiver add.
signals.quote: I agree that he had an excellent camp

signals.claim: Lane (likely the 'Jalen' Quinn named) may take on deep-ball duties that McLaurin handled.
signals.note: Deep-play speed could earn him more snaps, but the name is a caption guess and the role is not defined.
signals.quote: You feel some of the deep plays with Jalen.

signals.claim: Burks could take on some of McLaurin's role, depending on his health.
signals.note: Quinn named him among the deep-speed options, but his injury status is unresolved.

signals.claim: Daniels will keep running scrambles and play-action keepers, and the team will emphasize out-of-pocket plays.
signals.note: His rushing upside stays in the plan, though Quinn wants cleaner reads and more consistency.
signals.quote: I'm expecting, you know, his out of pocket, you know, plays to continue

topics.detail: Quinn expects smaller tweaks, not a new system or new plays. The goal is a more streamlined, decisive and precise execution, and he said there will be 'no more trial' at this point.
Quinn said the line's performance fell below the team's standard in both pass and run blocking. He will keep looking for the right interior combination.
He wants better pre-snap communication and urgency, and fewer explosive plays allowed in the pass game. He said players who don't meet the standard could lose reps.
Quinn said the team has a plus turnover margin (+6) but isn't converting it into wins. He cited a slow start against San Francisco and a stronger second half, and a chance to win the division.
